data.name: CompactConfirmBody
data.value:
The disk is rewritten without its unused blocks, then replaces the original; its content does not change. Space freed by files deleted in the guest is only given back if the guest reported it: machine running, “Report free space (TRIM)” (Guest tools), on a disk with the “Discard” option.
The volume needs as much free space as the disk takes up, for the time of the copy.

data.name: LiveSnapshotBody
data.value:
Each disk gets an overlay, and the machine writes to it from now on; the current image becomes its base image.
Memory is not captured: to the guest, going back will look like a power cut. The overlay is undone from the Disks section.

The content of {0} is written into {1}, then the overlay is deleted.
Nothing the guest has written is lost, but the snapshot ceases to exist: you will no longer be able to go back to it.

data.name: InstallToolsWindowsNoAgent
data.value:
WinQEMU will insert {0} into the machine's drive{1}. Then, in the guest, open that drive (“virtio-win”) in File Explorer and run, in this order:
1. virtio-win-guest-tools.exe (virtio drivers, clipboard); accept to trust Red Hat; 2. guest-agent\qemu-ga-x86_64.msi (the guest agent).
WinQEMU waits for the agent, then finishes on its own. It types nothing into Windows itself: Microsoft Defender takes a command typed in Run for an attack, and blocks it.

Choose it: WinQEMU will remember it for next time.

data.name: UsbHelpBody
data.value:
QEMU can only use USB devices that run Microsoft's generic WinUSB driver. Unlike VMware, it has no driver of its own that could take a device away from Windows.
To put a device on WinUSB: 1. Download Zadig (zadig.akeo.ie), the standard tool for this. 2. Run it. In the Options menu, check “List All Devices”: without it, Zadig does not show devices that already have a driver. 3. In the drop-down list at the top, choose the device. Check that “USB ID” shows the same numbers as this menu (for example 0781 559C). 4. In the middle, the left box shows the current driver (for example USBSTOR); the right one, the driver to install: set it to WinUSB with its small arrows. 5. Click the big “Replace Driver” button and wait until it finishes (about a minute). 6. Open this menu again: the device connects.
As long as it is on WinUSB, Windows no longer uses it itself: a USB drive no longer appears in File Explorer. To give it back: Device Manager, right-click the device, “Uninstall device” with “Attempt to remove the driver for this device” checked, then unplug it and plug it back in.
Never do this for the keyboard, mouse or Bluetooth this PC needs.

data.name: TemplateMakeBody
data.value:
A template is not started: it is deployed. Each deployment creates a new machine in seconds, a linked clone that shares the template's disks and only stores what it changes.
The template's snapshots are frozen as well. You can convert it back to a virtual machine at any time; the machines already deployed keep working.
